summary: This note is a collection of excerpts from the Wikipedia article on the Pacific War, covering Axis allies and collaborationist forces, the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and the debate over them, the Soviet invasion of Manchuria, the Allied strategic bombing and blockade of Japan, Japanese submarine and naval losses, the Japanese move into Indochina, the Battle of West Hunan, Operation U-Go against India, and the dating of the war's start. It also notes the U.S. official policy treating Thailand as a country forced into Japanese actions rather than a former enemy.
one_line: Wikipedia excerpts on the Pacific War, covering Axis allies, the atomic bombings, the Soviet invasion of Manchuria, Allied bombing and blockade of Japan, and the war's start date.
key_facts: Thailand quickly formed a temporary alliance with Japan in 1941, as Japanese forces were already invading the peninsula of southern Thailand.
On 6 August 1945, the U.S. dropped an atomic bomb on the Japanese city of Hiroshima, the first nuclear attack in history.
On 9 August 1945, the U.S. dropped another atomic bomb on Nagasaki, the last nuclear attack in history.
More than 140,000–240,000 people died as a direct result of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki bombings.
The Manchurian Strategic Offensive Operation began on 9 August 1945 with the Soviet invasion of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo.
On 9–10 March 1945, about 100,000 people were killed in a conflagration caused by an incendiary attack on Tokyo.
The Potsdam Declaration was issued on 26 July 1945 by Harry S. Truman, Chiang Kai-shek and Winston Churchill, threatening Japan with "prompt and utter destruction" if it did not surrender.
U.S. submarines accounted for 56% of the Japanese merchantmen sunk, and mines or aircraft destroyed most of the rest.
U.S. submariners claimed 28% of Japanese warships destroyed.
Japan signed a military alliance with Germany and Italy on 27 September 1940, becoming one of the three Axis Powers.
In September 1940, Japan decided to cut China's only land line to the outside world by seizing Indochina, which was controlled by Vichy France.
Chinese forces totaled 110,000 men in 20 divisions in the Battle of West Hunan, supported by about 400 aircraft.
Japan's Operation U-Go, an offensive into India, was advocated by Lieutenant General Renya Mutaguchi, commander of the Fifteenth Army.

It is generally considered that the Pacific War began on 7/8 December 1941, when Japan invaded Thailand and attacked British possessions and U.S. bases in Hawaii, Wake Island, Guam and the Philippines.
The Second Sino-Japanese War began on 7 July 1937, and the Japanese invasion of Manchuria occurred on 19 September 1931; some historians date the Asian conflict from these events.

entities.name: Thailand
entities.role: authoritarian Axis-aligned government that formed a temporary alliance with Japan in 1941

entities.name: Manchukuo
entities.role: Japanese puppet state consisting of most of Manchuria, invaded by the Soviets in August 1945

entities.name: Mengjiang
entities.role: Japanese puppet state consisting of parts of Inner Mongolia

entities.name: Hiroshima
entities.role: Japanese city hit by the first atomic bomb on 6 August 1945

entities.name: Nagasaki
entities.role: Japanese city hit by the second atomic bomb on 9 August 1945

entities.name: Harry S. Truman
entities.role: President of the United States who issued the Potsdam Declaration and warned Japan in a press release after the Hiroshima bombing

entities.name: Chiang Kai-shek
entities.role: President of the Nationalist Government of China who co-issued the Potsdam Declaration

entities.name: Winston Churchill
entities.role: Prime Minister of Great Britain who co-issued the Potsdam Declaration

entities.name: Curtis LeMay
entities.role: United States Army Air Forces General who oversaw U.S. strategic bombing in the Pacific

entities.name: Richard B. Frank
entities.role: historian who wrote that a Soviet invasion of Japan was never likely due to insufficient naval capability

entities.name: George H.W. Bush
entities.role: future U.S. president rescued by submarines after being downed as a flier

entities.name: Renya Mutaguchi
entities.role: Lieutenant General and commander of the Japanese Fifteenth Army who advocated Operation U-Go

entities.name: He Yingqin
entities.role: commander-in-chief of Chinese forces in the Battle of West Hunan

entities.name: Potsdam Declaration
entities.role: 1945 ultimatum outlining Japan's terms of surrender as agreed at the Potsdam Conference

entities.name: Operation Starvation
entities.role: LeMay-led operation in which Japan's inland waterways were extensively mined by air

entities.name: Operation Downfall
entities.role: planned invasion of Japan that the atomic bombs helped avoid

entities.name: Operation U-Go
entities.role: Japanese offensive into India codenamed by the Japanese, across the frontier toward Imphal and Kohima

entities.name: Battle of West Hunan
entities.role: 1945 campaign in which Chinese forces achieved a decisive victory against Japanese forces

entities.name: Kwantung Army
entities.role: Japanese army whose rapid defeat by the Soviets is argued to be a significant factor in Japan's surrender

entities.name: Vichy France
entities.role: regime controlling Indochina in 1940 before the Japanese seized it

entities.name: Imphal
entities.role: Manipur city where British Fourteenth Army units concentrated in April 1944 against Japanese attacks

entities.name: Kohima
entities.role: Nagaland town to which a Japanese division advanced, cutting the main road to Imphal
